# LazarusDeveloper (dashboard mu460o3b, 2026-09-16: "release new compilers for
# all platforms").  All eight targets this fork publishes shipped in ONE cut,
# from ONE source commit, in ONE dist commit.
# This file is the authoritative answer to "which platforms have v59".
# Per-platform detail lives in dist/<target>/VERSION.txt and inside each tarball.

source_commit: 5c89c538b8fb1f00c83fb5cabd9260f6e71caba4
compiler_fix:  55e687f581  (GOD, 2026-09-16 -- the mechanism: compiler/tgobj.pas,
                            hlcgobj.pas, ncgbas.pas, nbas.pas, pstatmnt.pas)
               5c89c538b8  (Otto, 2026-09-17 -- statement ownership, escape sweep,
                            every source statement list; same five files)
merge:         14e0f0f334  (55e687f581 landed on main by MERGE, so the sha GOD

parent:        v58 (dedf242c696a543f9626e2839ced40876478a98a)

WHAT CHANGED IN v59 -- A COM INTERFACE TEMP DIES WITH ITS STATEMENT
  A function that returns a COM interface, called where its result is never
  stored in a variable ("Giver.Need.o.DoWork;"), leaves the reference in a
  hidden temp.  Up to v58 that temp was released only when the ROUTINE exited
  (or when the compiler happened to recycle the slot), so the object stayed
  checked out long past its line -- a holder that should have handed its object
  back at the semicolon kept it until the end of the procedure.  v59 releases it
  at the end of the source statement that produced it, the way Delphi does.

  Two commits carry it, and the second one is why the first did not ship alone:

    55e687f581  (GOD, 2026-09-16)  the mechanism.  A temp knows it holds a COM
                interface (tgobj), a slot still holding one is never recycled
                under a second result in the same statement, and tcgblocknode
                releases the statement's temps after every statement of a
                begin..end block.

    5c89c538b8  (Otto, 2026-09-17)  three holes measured on that build with
                the two matrices added in tests/test/ (tintfstmttemp1.pp, 32
                corners; tintfstmttemp2.pp, 28 corners), closed before anything
                shipped:
                  * a statement nested inside another -- the body of a
                    with/if/while/case whose EXPRESSION produced the temp --
                    released its parent's temp.  `with Giver.Need.o do begin
                    A; B end` ran B on a freed object (measured: the owner's
                    refcount hit zero after A).  Each temp now records which
                    source statement allocated it and a statement releases
                    only its own, never an enclosing one's.
                  * exit, break, continue, goto and raise LEAKED the temp for
                    good: the routine-exit sweep had been trimmed to skip
                    temps whose statement-end release existed, and those
                    escapes never reach that release.  Measured: every one of
                    them leaked exactly one object.  The sweep covers every
                    managed temp again; a slot that was already released is
                    nil and costs one compare, one that was abandoned is
                    released at routine exit, and nothing is released twice.
                  * repeat..until bodies, try/finally/except bodies and
                    case-else lists kept the old routine-exit lifetime, because
                    only begin..end had been marked as a source statement list.

  What does NOT change: an interface stored in a variable, field, array or
  Result lives exactly as long as it always did.  Two results used in one
  statement are both alive until that statement ends.  A temp produced by an
  if/while condition, a case selector or a with expression stays alive through
  the branch, the loop body or the with block and is released when that
  statement ends.

  COMPILER BINARY ONLY.  No RTL change, no package change, no PPU FORMAT change
  (the unit files' own header/version are untouched), so every existing unit
  set for this target stays valid and does not need rebuilding.  Code compiled
  by v59 simply releases these temps sooner.

WHY THERE IS A SECOND COMMIT, IN ONE PARAGRAPH
  The release was measured before it was cut.  The 55e687f581 build passes
  GOD's own holder test and fails 31 of the 60 corners in the two matrices
  written for this release: three objects leaked (one per abandoned statement
  -- exit, break, continue, goto, raise), four use-after-free corners (a
  nested block freeing its parent statement's object), and six statement
  lists still on the old lifetime.  v58 fails 35 of the same 60 the OLD way
  (everything released at routine exit) and leaks nothing.  Shipping the
  first build would have traded a too-long lifetime for a leak and a dangling
  pointer, which is a regression even where the reported case passes.  The
  hardening keeps GOD's mechanism and its data structures and adds one
  integer per temp: which statement allocated it.

HOW EACH BINARY WAS SHOWN TO CARRY THE FIX -- BY RUNNING IT
  Every one of these compilers reports "3.3.1".  The version string cannot tell
  v58 from v59, so it was never used as evidence.  The discriminating test is
  the pair of self-checking programs added to tests/test/ with this release:

    tintfstmttemp1.pp  32 corners: free proc, method, nested proc, main body,
                       if/for/while/repeat/with bodies, two temps in one
                       statement, a temp passed as a parameter, a temp made in
                       a routine that raised, a stored interface.
    tintfstmttemp2.pp  28 corners: exit/break/continue/goto/raise mid-statement,
                       a raise from a nested block, a with/if/while/case whose
                       expression made the temp with a nested block under it,
                       repeat/try/finally/except/on/case-else bodies, an
                       unentered block, and destroyed == created at the end.

  Both were compiled BY each shipped compiler and the products RUN -- natively
  for x86_64-linux and the i386 output, under qemu-user for every ARM binary
  (native and cross), under wine64 for win64 -- and every run prints
  checks=32 fails=0 and checks=28 fails=0 created=27 destroyed=27 live=0.  The
  same programs on the published v58 compiler print 23 and 12 failures; on the
  unhardened 55e687f581 build 2/3 and 28.  A gate that cannot fail proves
  nothing; this one says NO in both directions.

  The two darwin rows are the exception, and saying so is the point: nothing
  here executes a Mach-O.  Their evidence is (a) the same source, run on the
  same CPU, as a Linux-hosted binary, (b) the recompiled-unit count, and (c)
  the single-axis section triage in each VERSION.txt, whose control is a v58
  rebuild made today that reproduces the shipped v58 section for section.

THE ARM NATIVE GATE, so the next person does not misread a 24/25
  dist/ppu-truncation-check.sh runs the compiler under a 1 GB address-space cap
  (a real, measured OOM guard, cy1127).  A 32-bit ARM guest under qemu-user
  binfmt cannot START under that cap -- "Unable to find a guest_base to satisfy
  all guest address mapping requirements 00000000-ffffffff" -- so the gate
  scores the native ppcarm 24/25 with "the compiler rejects a GOOD unit".  That
  is the emulator: the PUBLISHED v58 ppcarm scores exactly the same 24/25 under
  the default cap, and both score 25/25 with TRUNCCHECK_VMCAP_KB=8388608.  The
  arm CROSS compiler from the same source scores 25/25 under the default cap.

UNITS ARE UNCHANGED ON EVERY TARGET.  git diff --stat dedf242c69 5c89c538b8 --
rtl/ packages/ is EMPTY: RTL and package SOURCE did not move between v58 and
v59, only compiler/ (five files, +149/-16 across the two commits) and tests/.
The PPU format did not move either.  Every units tarball this fork has ever
published pairs with a v59 compiler exactly as it paired with v58.

WHO CAN STILL CLOSE WHAT
  * real Windows: v58 ran on real hardware; v59 has not.  Lars routes the
    real-Windows smoke non-blocking to Steve as usual.
  * physical ARM silicon: never, for any release (board question
    q_1789125036770_2jfmr9 still open).
  * a Mac: no scheduled queue reaches one (darwin_real_hardware_proof).

================================================================================
ADDENDUM 2026-09-17 (cy1134) -- v59 HAS NOW RUN ON REAL WINDOWS, AND THE v58
CONTROL FAILED THERE
================================================================================
Nothing above is rewritten.  The two paragraphs this supersedes are left
verbatim where they are, so every hash they quote stays valid: the win64
RUNTIME note ("wine is NOT Windows; v58 ran on real Windows (2026-09-12), v59
has not yet.") and the first bullet of WHO CAN STILL CLOSE WHAT.  Both were
true when this manifest was cut at 01:29Z.  They stopped being true at 02:08Z.

WHO RAN IT, AND ON WHAT
  Morgan (TheOperator), answering the board question this release shipped with
  -- q_1789609512871_q8gds7, answer a_1789610806475_cbqi0r, 2026-09-17.
  Native Windows, no emulation layer: Windows Server 2025 Datacenter, version
  string "Microsoft Windows [Version 10.0.26100.1742]", 64-bit, and
  HKCU\Software\Wine absent.  It IS a Hyper-V virtual machine (Win32_Computer-
  System Manufacturer "Microsoft Corporation", Model "Virtual Machine",
  HypervisorPresent True; host CPU AMD Ryzen Threadripper 1950X) -- a real
  Windows kernel and the real Win64 API on virtualized hardware.  That is the
  distinction this addendum rests on: a VM runs the genuine OS, wine
  reimplements it.

THE BYTES HE RAN WERE THE PUBLISHED ONES
  All five inputs pulled unauthenticated from
  raw.githubusercontent.com/adaloveless/vibepascal/main, hashed BEFORE running,
  and every one MATCHED the numbers printed above:
    vibepascal-v59-5c89c538b8-win64-bin.tar.gz  3433324 B
                                   md5 7979ccc69051fef132bdc86c86833785
    vibepascal-v52-win64-units.tar.gz         104069603 B
                                   md5 cc8d2e1f4456a363fd40c07a487a281c
    vibepascal-v58-dedf242c69-win64-bin.tar.gz  3463476 B
                                   md5 5d0814f675a58bf2fc40535bfa86e7ca
    VP\bin\ppcx64.exe      5054976 B  md5 bec75bee2d6c4b105734c328216488d8 (v59)
    VP\bin\ppcx64-v58.exe  5049856 B  md5 447b4e500c5525a7fd89b21a6f7dd303 (v58)
  plus tintfstmttemp1.pp (6468 B, md5 7cdbce4cbddc67c381d332912f2964e7) and
  tintfstmttemp2.pp (7356 B, md5 651e8cb568fcdf430751056c4adb825b).
  Nothing was installed: one scratch folder, no PATH change, no registry
  change, deleted afterwards.  Both compilers read the same VP\bin\fpc.cfg, and
  each matrix ran in its own empty subfolder -- the compiler created
  units\x86_64-win64 under each CWD by itself.

WHICH COMPILER SAID IT (CHECK 0)
  VP\bin\ppcx64.exe     -iV -> 3.3.1    -iD -> 2026/09/17   (v59)
  VP\bin\ppcx64-v58.exe -iV -> 3.3.1    -iD -> 2026/09/11   (v58 control)
  The date is the identity: 2026/09/17 is the day this release was cut.

THE RESULT, AND THE CONTROL THAT MAKES IT MEAN SOMETHING
  v59, real Windows:
    tintfstmttemp1.exe  exit 0   no FAIL lines
                        checks=32 fails=0 created=25          VERDICT:PASS
    tintfstmttemp2.exe  exit 0   no FAIL lines
                        checks=28 fails=0 created=27 destroyed=27 live=0
                                                              VERDICT:PASS
  v58, the SAME programs on the SAME box, in a separate folder:
    tintfstmttemp1.exe  exit 1   23 FAIL lines
                        checks=32 fails=23 created=25         VERDICT:FAIL
    tintfstmttemp2.exe  exit 1   12 FAIL lines
                        checks=28 fails=12 created=27 destroyed=27 live=0
                                                              VERDICT:FAIL
  The first v58 failure reads exactly as predicted before the run:
    FAIL: free proc: temp released at end of its statement  (live=1)
  and the 23 + 12 counts are the same counts wine64 produced here.  THE
  CONTROLS SPLIT: the harness says NO on v58 and YES on v59 on real Windows, so
  the PASS is a measurement and not an artifact of a gate that cannot fail.
  Every count, exit code and hash Morgan reported matches what this manifest
  predicted; nothing differed.

WHAT THIS CLOSES
  The win64 row of WHO CAN STILL CLOSE WHAT.  For v59 on real Win64, "wine is
  not Windows" is no longer an open caveat -- the published bytes ran on a real
  Windows kernel and the fix is present there.

WHAT IT DOES NOT CLOSE
  * The hardware is virtualized (Hyper-V).  Real kernel, real API, not bare
    metal.  Steve's box, if it runs, is a second independent data point.
  * Physical ARM silicon: still never, for any release
    (q_1789125036770_2jfmr9, still open).
  * darwin: unchanged and still the honest exception -- no scheduled queue on
    this site reaches a Mac, and nothing here has ever executed a Mach-O.
  * The two darwin VERSION.txt files and every other per-platform VERSION.txt
    are deliberately NOT touched by this addendum.  They mirror bytes already
    inside published tarballs.

================================================================================
ADDENDUM 2026-09-17 (cy1147) -- READ THIS BEFORE QUOTING THE ARM SILICON RESULT
================================================================================
  VibePascal ran on physical ARM silicon for the first time today.  THE BYTES
  THAT RAN WERE v58, NOT v59.  The aarch64-linux entry above is unchanged and
  still correct as written: v59's ARM runtime evidence is qemu-aarch64-static
  only.  This note exists so nobody reads today's win as covering the tarball
  this manifest points at.

  WHAT WAS PROVEN, AND ON WHAT.  Wes (SiteManager_gx10-3c9a), a native aarch64
  Linux box, 2026-09-17 16:24-16:26 UTC, on the PUBLISHED v58 bytes:
    vibepascal-v58-dedf242c69-aarch64-linux-bin.tar.gz
       1508828 B  md5 f0e5da8a60468be2ef2e390747bbdb87
       member bin/ppca64  md5 78c729e8addfb7a8e80ddb245ca57049
    vibepascal-v52-aarch64-linux-units.tar.gz
      84809752 B  md5 a8e82e441275abb2bc75a1554f2d7c56
  Extract both into one empty dir, nothing installed, then: uname -m aarch64;
  ppca64 -iV 3.3.1; ppca64 -iSP aarch64; compile a SysUtils + Classes program
  against the published unit tree, exit 0; run it, exit 0, correct output.
  file(1) says both the compiler AND its output are ARM aarch64 ELF, so the
  codegen is native too.  Full detail, including his qemu-binfmt disclosure and
  his negative control, is in the cy1147 addendum to dist/RELEASE-v58.txt.

  WHAT THAT DOES AND DOES NOT TRANSFER TO v59, stated precisely because the
  halves differ:
  * THE UNIT SET TRANSFERS EXACTLY.  v58 and v59 pair with the SAME units
    tarball -- vibepascal-v52-aarch64-linux-units.tar.gz, md5 a8e82e44... --
    byte-identical, not merely equivalent.  So "the published units are real,
    complete enough to build a SysUtils + Classes program, and correctly laid
    out for -Fu/-Fl on hardware" is proven for v59 as well.  That was the part
    that had never been true before: four aarch64 releases shipped a compiler
    with NO units, so on a clean box they could not compile one line.
  * THE COMPILER BINARY DOES NOT TRANSFER.  v59's ppca64 is a different binary
    (md5 01d7bf8343053475c71d3c3c5acabf78, 5181472 B) built from a different
    source commit (5c89c538b8), and it has never executed on ARM hardware.  The
    v58 -> v59 delta is not cosmetic: it is the COM interface function-result
    temp lifetime work (GOD's 55e687f581 plus the cy1133 statement-ownership and
    escape-sweep hardening).  That is codegen and lifetime behaviour, which is
    exactly the class of change a "it surely still compiles hello" argument is
    worst at covering.  We do not ship on "surely".

  SO, PLAINLY: as of today the CURRENT published aarch64-linux compiler has no
  hardware proof; the immediately previous one does, and the unit set both share
  does.  Anyone quoting the ARM result must say v58.

  WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: the identical sequence against the v59 bin tarball
  (1500778 B, md5 6405ce654b566fe0d31fc6c9b347eadd) with the same v52 units.  It
  is roughly a two-minute job for anyone who has already done the v58 run -- one
  tarball swapped, four commands re-run.  Asked of Wes as an explicitly OPTIONAL
  follow-up the same hour this gap was found; he had already been told he was
  done, and he is not obliged to.  If it is not taken up, this paragraph stands
  and v59 aarch64 stays qemu-only in every document we publish.

  32-bit ARM (arm-linux / armhf) is untouched by any of this and remains
  unproven on hardware, with no candidate machine anywhere in the fleet.
